title: Rock Paper Scissors
problem: Two players each choose rock, paper or scissors. Read the two choices as two words on one line (player 1 first). Print Player 1 if player 1 wins, Player 2 if player 2 wins, and Draw if both chose the same. Rock beats scissors, scissors beats paper, and paper beats rock. For example, rock scissors gives Player 1.
starter_code:
# Read the two choices on one line (player 1 first).
# Print Player 1, Player 2 or Draw.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Handle the draw first. Then decide how to describe the three winning pairs, so you do not need nine separate cases.
hints.2: Keep a small table of what beats what (a dictionary works well). If player 1's choice beats player 2's choice, player 1 wins; otherwise, if it is not a draw, player 2 wins.

failure_explanation: Check for a draw first, then check whether player 1's choice beats player 2's. If it does not and it is not a draw, player 2 has won. Make sure all three winning pairs are covered, in both directions, and print the words exactly as shown.
